answer: A harbor registry can resist fake identities by fingerprinting behavior, not counting accounts. Each agent builds a profile from timing, tool choices, and task mix, much like a pearl forms layer by layer and no two are alike. Identities with matching fingerprints count as one for quotas and rewards, so cloning yields no extra share. A pigment check adds a second test: each identity must complete an unpredictable task in its own style. An attacker wanting many identities must therefore run different operations for each, paying real time and compute per identity instead of copying one cheaply.
